routing_warnings.description: The requirement to delete proposed removals in suggesting mode and leave a rationale comment is a tracked-editing and documentation obligation rather than a change to the curation criteria.
The clauses about introducing new questions, creating a new category, and improving question wording concern content modernization rather than selection and organization of the existing inventory.
The requirement for editorial review before implementing proposed additions or removals belongs to the independent editorial-approval Requirement.
The instruction to make actual edits in the Google Doc using suggestion mode and comments concerns the tracked manuscript-editing workflow.
The instructional scaffolding left in the submitted manuscript is execution evidence for manuscript cleanliness rather than question-content modernization.
The reference to a nonexistent book-wide note is execution evidence for manuscript reference completeness.
The client's findings about AI-workflow scaffolding, submission speed, detection results, and insufficient original work concern the original-authorship requirement.
The instructional scaffolding left in the submission is failure evidence for manuscript cleanliness, not for the layered answer structure.
The reference to a nonexistent book-wide note is failure evidence for manuscript reference completeness.
The AI-detection and originality findings concern the original-authorship and limited-AI Requirement.
The instruction to incorporate US, India, and other market differences throughout planned chapters primarily changes the separate global-perspective Requirement.

The editorial findings about AI-generated scaffolding, detection results, and insufficient original professional judgment concern the authorship and limited-AI Requirement rather than the substantive AI interview-preparation chapter.

The AI-workflow scaffolding, detection results, and lack of original analysis are concrete failure evidence for the original-authorship and limited-AI Requirement, not for the subject matter of the first-time-leader chapter.
The reference to a nonexistent book-wide note is failure evidence for manuscript reference completeness rather than for this chapter's subject-matter Requirement.
The instruction to use a leadership-specific approach rather than basic preparation advice applies specifically to the pre-interview preparation chapter.
The instructional scaffolding left in the submission is failure evidence for reader-facing manuscript cleanliness, not target-reader alignment.
The reference to a nonexistent book-wide note is failure evidence for manuscript reference completeness.
The client's originality and AI-assistance findings concern the original-authorship Requirement.
The clause reporting instructional workflow text left in the submission also provides target-specific failure evidence for reader-facing manuscript cleanliness.
The clause reporting a reference to a nonexistent book-wide note provides target-specific failure evidence for manuscript reference completeness.
